notes: This patch matches the reference fix almost exactly, using unexported Token methods in place of free functions, and it covers every brace check in both the dispenser and the parser (including the address suffix check and the '{}' check). Its tests are focused and cover the dispenser, the parser and full adaptation; the only omission is the doc-comment updates the reference made.

Matches the reference: it adds unquoted-brace helpers (as Token methods) and applies them at every structural brace check in the dispenser and parser, including the address-suffix check and the '{}' check, with thorough tests at the dispenser, parser and adapter levels; the only gap is that the doc comments are not updated.

Fixes the reported root-module for_each case by returning a slice instead of a ConfigResource-keyed map. However, it still applies the parent-overrides-child rule per ConfigResource rather than per resource instance. A parent import of one instance (e.g. module.child["x"] or a["k1"]) therefore silently drops the child's imports for every other instance, the same class of silent-drop bug the reference avoids by deduplicating in expandResourceImports. The unit test even locks in this over-dropping behavior, consistent with failing 2 of 3 hidden tests.

Fixes the reported same-module for_each case by returning a slice instead of a map, but it still applies parent-over-child overrides per ConfigResource rather than per resource instance after expansion. As a result, child-module imports for other instances (or other module instances) are silently dropped whenever a parent imports any instance of that resource, which is likely why 2 of 3 hidden tests fail; the added unit test also locks in that coarse override behaviour.

Works and passes the hidden tests by rewriting the page and section paths: it walks the ancestor sections, applies their slugs, and re-parses the remapped path, which correctly covers nested sections, bundles, taxonomies and terms and respects disablePathToLower. Re-parsing a synthetic path through PathParser is heavier and more fragile than the reference's cleaner descriptor change (a Dir field); the docs update and integration tests for sections, taxonomies and terms are relevant and well chosen.

Walks the ancestor sections, builds a slug-adjusted branch prefix, and re-parses the page and section paths to fix section, nested-section, leaf-bundle, taxonomy and term URLs, with good tests and a fitting docs update; re-parsing full paths per page is heavier and more fragile than the reference's direct Dir computation, and could misbehave for file-less or content-adapter pages.

It rewrites the single scenario into a 1/1 shared-iterations scenario after consolidation, keeping exec, env, tags and options, and it rejects multiple scenarios and the vus, iterations, duration and stage flags. It does not strip shortcuts from the config, script and env layers before the merge, so something like K6_DURATION silently drops the script's scenarios and `default` runs instead. It also ignores the execution-segment flags, and it changes two existing cloud tests to use --once, so their non-once coverage is lost.

Rewrites the single scenario to shared-iterations 1/1 after consolidation, preserving exec, env, tags and options, and rejects multiple scenarios and shortcut flags, which covers the core feature. It misses lower-layer shortcuts such as K6_ITERATIONS or K6_DURATION wiping the script's scenarios during the merge, ignores execution-segment flags, and turns an unset exec into an explicit "default". It also adds --once to existing cloud tests, which drops their non-once coverage.

The sentinel-error approach does enable early and multiple returns, but it breaks the existing `{{ return fn args }}` syntax: `return add . 42` now needs parentheses, and something like `return dict "a" 1` silently returns the wrong value. It also lets a bare return in an included `{{ template }}` abort the whole outer template, ignores return values outside partials instead of raising an error, and makes a bare return in a partial yield nil instead of the output rendered so far. Existing tests were rewritten to hide these regressions, and the broad docs edits go beyond the task's scope.

The sentinel-return mechanism lets partials return early from any branch, but it breaks the existing `{{ return add . 42 }}` syntax, and the candidate edited the existing test and docs to require parentheses instead of preserving it. A bare `{{ return }}` inside `{{ template }}` aborts the whole outer template rather than stopping at the template boundary. A return with a value in a non-partial is silently swallowed instead of reported as an error, and pipelines with `return` in a non-final position are not validated.

It does keep the parentheses by lifting a bare NumberLiteral into a wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr, but it also forces `Duration=true`, so `(5)` prints as `(5s)` instead of round-tripping exactly. The new node's position range excludes the parens because it starts at the number and has no EndPos, which diverges from the reference AST and fails the hidden test. It adds an unneeded panic default branch plus extra validation and comment churn, though its own printer, parse and visitor tests are reasonably thorough.

Wrapping the bare NumberLiteral in a unary-plus wrapped DurationExpr and printing unary plus without the sign match the reference approach. But the candidate also forces `Duration = true` on the literal, so `foo offset (5)` prints as `(5s)` rather than round-tripping to `(5)`. It adds a panicking default branch, rewrites the `positive_duration_expr` validation and edits an unrelated `ast.go` comment, and it fails both the hidden test and the package suite.
